To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) We design a new framework for computing SVD of matrices that are *implicitly* defined, and apply it to several GRL problems, including node classification and link prediction, (ii) Our framework can be applied in two ways: (a) It can initialize a deep model that is architected as linear everywhere, but behaves non-linear when its parameters reside at a hyperplane, (b) It can initialize and train a model that is architured as non-linear almost everywhere

1) SVD can be used to train GRL tasks, 2) SVD can initialize deeper models, 3) SVD can train deeper models within a handful of epochs, 4) SVD can outperform SOTA models, and 5) SVD can do all of the above hundreds of times faster, while using only a fraction of memory, than SOTA models
1. SVD of *Implicitly* defined Matrices can be computed, and 2. This can be applied to Graph Representation Learning tasks to yield SOTA performance with significantly reduced training cost.

the following: - Can we train a GRL model in closed-form, without calculating gradients? - Can we train the model in a single epoch?
- Implicit SVD: We derive an SVD-based framework that computes SVO of matrices that are implicitly defined, i.e., we do not calculate entries of the matrix, but instead, we calculate its SVD.

we have designed a framework that computes the SVD of a matrix $\mathbf M$ without explicitly storing $\mathbf M$, which we apply to several GRL problems, and show that our approach can train hundreds of times faster, while maintaining comparable test empirical performance.
our method is a new algorithm that can be used to train a model on graphs.
we propose a novel approach that can train GRL models faster than state-of-art methods, with comparable performance.

, we have shown that SVD is an effective tool for GRL.
we propose a novel framework for GRL that is computationally tractable and competitive in performance.
we propose a novel framework that allows us to train a GRL model in a single epoch, and without computing the gradients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for some problems, SVD can be used to train a model in one step.
SVD, as a closed-form solution to convex problems, can be applied to GRL tasks, and that SVD can be used to initialize a deep GRL model, which can then be fine tuned within a few epochs.
SVD can initialize models to a point that is competitive with state-of-the-art models, and can be used as a drop-in replacement for the initialization of GRL models.
